title: Yeonmi Park Details Horrific Effects of North Korean Starvation

recap:
Yeonmi Park sits down with Joe to discuss one of the most haunting topics imaginable: the systematic starvation of North Korea's population. This isn't abstract geopolitical talk. This is a firsthand account from someone who lived through it as a child and watched her country collapse under the weight of a regime that cares infinitely more about its military and maintaining power than keeping its own people alive.

What makes this conversation particularly intense is how Park breaks down the mechanics of why North Korea starves. It's not just bad luck or natural disaster. The government actively hoards resources, prioritizes the military industrial complex, and uses food as a weapon of control. People in the capital get more access than those in rural areas. Political prisoners and their families get nothing. It's engineered suffering.

Park doesn't hold back when describing what she witnessed as a kid. The scale of death, the desperation, the way parents had to make impossible choices about which children they could feed. She talks about cannibalism becoming so common that the regime had to actually execute people for it because it was destabilizing the social order. That's how bad it got.

What's equally disturbing is how the North Korean propaganda machine keeps people completely in the dark about the outside world. Most North Koreans have no idea that other countries have food, wealth, and freedom. They're taught that everyone everywhere else is suffering worse than they are. When Park finally escaped and saw what the rest of the world looked like, it fundamentally shattered her entire understanding of reality.

The conversation also touches on why the international community has such a hard time addressing this. China props up the regime. Sanctions are limited. And North Korea's government is so hostile to outside help that even humanitarian aid is nearly impossible to deliver. Park emphasizes that the solution isn't just about resources. It's about regime change and creating a scenario where the North Korean people can actually access the abundance that already exists in the world.
